purpose: Plan, execute, validate, and report bibliometric science-mapping studies (co-word, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, clustering, overlay and strategic diagrams, topic and burst detection) as session-bounded, evaluable work units with anti-rework sequencing.
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
subdomain node of Bibliometrics, Scientometrics and Research Evaluation
the consumer is a knowledge-searcher meta-KB locating WHERE and HOW to map scientific knowledge structure
a single mapping pipeline over one corpus is the unit of work
exclusions: raw citation-impact indicators and rankings (h-index, JIF) except as map inputs
general social-network theory beyond collaboration mapping

competency_questions.question: Which analysis unit and scope answer a given science-mapping question?
How is the bibliographic data source chosen and justified for the scope?
What cleaning and disambiguation steps precede relation extraction?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SM_RECORD_CLEAN and SM_ENTITY_DISAMBIG present and ordered

competency_questions.question: Which mapping tool fits the chosen relations and normalization?
How are conceptual (co-word) and social (co-authorship) structures extracted?
Which citation-based relations map the research front vs the intellectual base?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SM_BIBCOUPLING and SM_COCITATION present and distinguished

competency_questions.question: How is hyperauthorship handled in collaboration networks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SM_COAUTHOR records full vs fractional counting rule

competency_questions.question: How do bibliographic coupling and co-citation differ in what they reveal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: similarity edge between SM_BIBCOUPLING and SM_COCITATION explains the contrast

competency_questions.question: Which normalization measure and threshold turn counts into an interpretable network?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SM_NORMALIZATION and SM_THRESHOLD_PRUNE present with method records

competency_questions.question: How are clusters detected and classified into strategic themes?
How is the map laid out and its partition stability assessed over time?
How are clusters labeled, visualized, and reported reproducibly?
How are portfolio footprint and interdisciplinarity shown via overlay maps?
How are emerging topics and bursts detected and tracked dynamically?

glossary.definition: construction of spatial and network representations of the structure and dynamics of science from bibliographic data
mapping conceptual structure from co-occurrence of terms or keywords
linking documents by shared references (citing side)
linking cited items by frequency of being cited together (cited side)
a probabilistic normalization of co-occurrence proportional to expected co-occurrence under independence
partitioning a network into densely connected groups, often via modularity optimization
a centrality-density (Callon) plot classifying themes into four quadrants
projection of a corpus onto a fixed global base map of science
identification of abrupt surges in term or citation frequency (Kleinberg)
tracking of how themes emerge, merge, split, and decline across time slices
resolution of name ambiguity so a node represents a single real author
a science-mapping tool using association strength normalization and VOS clustering/layout

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed or experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established science-mapping and scientometrics literature and practice; no measured dataset supplied.
source_registry.citation_or_locator: de Solla Price 1963; Moed 2005; Ding, Rousseau & Wolfram 2014
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix the mapping question, the analysis unit (document, author, keyword, journal, institution), the time window, and the field delineation before any matrix is built.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when stakeholders redefine the field boundary or the question shifts from structure to dynamics

pros.claim: scope errors invalidate every downstream map
pros.example: a too-broad field delineation mixes unrelated communities into one cluster

cons.claim: over-constraining scope hides emerging interdisciplinary links
cons.example: narrow WoS category filter drops cross-field bridges

failure_modes: time window too short for trend detection
acceptance_tests: analysis unit answers the stated mapping question
time slices cover the trend horizon
revisit_triggers: field boundary disputed by domain experts
question changes from static structure to evolution

nodes.definition: Select and justify the bibliographic database (WoS, Scopus, Dimensions, OpenAlex, PubMed, Lens) whose coverage, field tags, and citation links match the scope.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when database coverage gaps or a new source materially change the visible network

pros.claim: source coverage determines which actors and links can ever appear
pros.example: Scopus vs WoS changes which regional journals are mapped

cons.claim: database field tags impose a hidden classification on the map
cons.example: WoS subject categories pre-bias overlay base maps

failure_modes: coverage bias mistaken for real structure
incompatible export schema for chosen tool
acceptance_tests: export contains fields needed for chosen unit (cited refs, keywords, addresses)
revisit_triggers: tool requires a field the export lacks

nodes.definition: Deduplicate records and normalize raw bibliographic fields (DOIs, references) to a consistent record set before any entity disambiguation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when duplicate or malformed records distort frequency counts

pros.claim: clean records keep co-occurrence counts honest
pros.example: removing duplicate records prevents inflated keyword frequencies

cons.claim: aggressive parsing can drop legitimate variant references
cons.example: strict DOI match discards reference strings without DOIs

failure_modes: reference parsing fails for non-standard formats
acceptance_tests: reference parse rate above documented threshold

nodes.definition: Resolve name ambiguity and variant forms for authors, institutions, and keywords so that nodes represent single real entities.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when disambiguation errors split or merge prominent actors

pros.claim: correct identities prevent split/merged nodes
pros.example: unifying 'J. Smith' variants prevents a fragmented author network

cons.claim: over-merging collapses distinct same-name authors
cons.example: merging two real homonymous authors creates a phantom hub

failure_modes: split identity hides a productive author
acceptance_tests: precision/recall of disambiguation estimated on a gold subset

nodes.definition: Build a term co-occurrence matrix from author/index keywords or extracted terms to map the conceptual and thematic structure of the field.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when keyword vocabulary drift changes the term space

pros.claim: reveals conceptual themes directly from author language
pros.example: co-word clusters expose research fronts before citation accrues

cons.claim: indexer or author vocabulary inconsistency biases themes
cons.example: uncontrolled keywords inflate spurious term links

failure_modes: term frequency threshold drops emerging terms

nodes.definition: Construct the co-authorship network linking authors, institutions, or countries that share publications to map the social and collaboration structure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when disambiguation revision changes who collaborates with whom

pros.claim: exposes collaboration communities and brokers
pros.example: country co-authorship maps reveal global research blocs

cons.claim: hyperauthorship inflates trivial co-authorship ties
cons.example: a 1000-author physics paper creates a dense false clique

acceptance_tests: full-counting vs fractional weighting decision recorded
giant-clique papers handled per documented rule

nodes.definition: Link documents or actors by the number of references they share, mapping the current research front based on common cited literature.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when reference parsing quality changes shared-reference counts

pros.claim: captures the active research front from the citing side
pros.example: recent papers cluster by shared bibliography before being cited

cons.claim: coupling is static once a paper is published
cons.example: cannot track how a front evolves after publication

failure_modes: review papers create artificial coupling hubs

nodes.definition: Link cited documents, authors, or journals by how often they are cited together, mapping the intellectual base and established knowledge structure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when citation window choice changes which references co-occur

pros.claim: reveals foundational works and schools of thought
pros.example: author co-citation maps the theoretical structure of a discipline

cons.claim: biased toward older, highly cited works
cons.example: recent influential work is invisible until citations accrue

nodes.definition: Convert raw co-occurrence and coupling counts into normalized similarity (association strength, cosine, Jaccard, Salton, inclusion index) to control for frequency effects.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the choice of similarity measure changes cluster membership materially

pros.claim: removes spurious size effects so weak actors are comparable
pros.example: association strength corrects for high-frequency keyword dominance

cons.claim: different measures yield different maps from the same data
cons.example: cosine vs association strength shift cluster boundaries

acceptance_tests: sensitivity of clusters to measure choice assessed

nodes.definition: Apply minimum frequency, minimum link strength, and top-N selection to reduce the network to an interpretable, stable backbone.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when threshold choice removes or admits whole communities

pros.claim: a clean backbone makes the map readable
pros.example: top-1000 terms by occurrence yields a legible VOSviewer map

cons.claim: thresholds silently delete emerging small clusters
cons.example: a high min-occurrence cut hides nascent research fronts

failure_modes: threshold removes the phenomenon of interest

nodes.definition: Partition the normalized network into clusters or communities using modularity (Louvain/Leiden), VOS clustering, hierarchical, or k-means to identify thematic or social groups.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when resolution parameter or algorithm choice changes the number or composition of clusters

pros.claim: clusters are the interpretable themes or communities of the map
pros.example: Leiden clusters reveal distinct subfields in a discipline map

cons.claim: modularity resolution limit hides small but real clusters
cons.example: default resolution merges two genuine subfields

nodes.definition: Compute a spatial layout (VOS mapping, force-directed, MDS) and render the map so distance encodes dissimilarity and clusters are visually separable.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when layout distortion misrepresents inter-cluster distances

pros.claim: good layout makes structure legible to humans
pros.example: VOSviewer distance-based layout shows theme adjacency at a glance

cons.claim: a 2D projection distorts high-dimensional similarity
cons.example: close-on-screen nodes may not be the most similar

acceptance_tests: stress or quality of projection reported

nodes.definition: Choose and configure the mapping tool (VOSviewer, CitNetExplorer, SciMAT, Gephi, bibliometrix/biblioshiny, Pajek) consistent with the chosen relations, normalization, and outputs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when tool defaults silently change normalization or clustering

pros.claim: the right tool encodes the right method by default
pros.example: VOSviewer defaults to association strength plus VOS clustering

cons.claim: hidden tool defaults bias the map without the analyst noticing
cons.example: Gephi default modularity resolution differs from a Leiden CLI

failure_modes: tool default normalization mismatches the intended method
acceptance_tests: tool defaults reconciled with intended method

nodes.definition: Project a corpus onto a fixed global base map of science (journal or category co-citation) to show a portfolio disciplinary footprint and interdisciplinarity.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the global base map is updated or recomputed

pros.claim: compares portfolios on a stable shared coordinate system
pros.example: overlay maps show a university disciplinary spread vs the world

cons.claim: a fixed base map ages and may misclassify new fields
cons.example: an outdated base map cannot place a newly emerged discipline

failure_modes: base map staleness misplaces emerging fields
journals unmapped to base categories are dropped
acceptance_tests: base map version and source recorded

nodes.definition: Detect latent topics from text (LDA, BERTopic, embeddings, direct-citation clustering) as an alternative or complement to keyword co-word themes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when topic-model hyperparameters change the number or coherence of topics

pros.claim: captures themes from full text beyond author keywords
pros.example: BERTopic finds sub-themes that index keywords miss

cons.claim: topic count and coherence are sensitive to hyperparameters
cons.example: LDA topic-number choice changes the thematic map

nodes.definition: Track how themes, communities, and topics emerge, merge, split, and die across time slices to map the dynamics of a field.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when time-slicing granularity changes the detected evolution

pros.claim: turns a static snapshot into a narrative of field development
pros.example: SciMAT thematic evolution shows a topic splitting into two

cons.claim: cluster matching across slices is ambiguous and method-dependent
cons.example: different matching rules show merge vs split for the same data

acceptance_tests: slicing scheme and matching rule recorded
cross-slice matching validated on a stable subset

nodes.definition: Detect sudden surges in term, citation, or topic frequency (Kleinberg burst detection, CiteSpace) to flag emerging research fronts and trends.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when burst model parameters change which terms are flagged

pros.claim: highlights fast-rising fronts ahead of cumulative counts
pros.example: burst detection flags a topic spiking before it dominates

cons.claim: burst parameters and end-of-window effects cause false signals
cons.example: a recent partial-year spike registers as a spurious burst

nodes.definition: Place clusters on a centrality-density (Callon) strategic diagram to classify themes as motor, basic/transversal, emerging/declining, or specialized/niche.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when centrality or density measure definitions change quadrant placement

pros.claim: classifies themes by maturity and importance for decisions
pros.example: the motor-themes quadrant shows where a field is well developed

cons.claim: quadrant boundaries are sensitive to centrality and density definitions
cons.example: a theme flips quadrant under a different density normalization

failure_modes: centrality measure mismatched to network type

nodes.definition: Assign meaningful, validated labels to clusters and topics using top terms, representative documents, and domain expertise, avoiding over-interpretation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when domain experts dispute a cluster label or coherence

pros.claim: labels make the map communicable and decision-relevant
pros.example: an expert-validated label turns cluster 7 into 'gene editing ethics'

cons.claim: naive top-term labels mislead non-expert readers
cons.example: a top-term label 'cell' hides a clinical-vs-battery ambiguity

failure_modes: label not traceable to cluster content
acceptance_tests: labels traceable to top terms and documents
expert validation of a sample of labels recorded

nodes.definition: Validate the map by testing sensitivity to method choices (counting, normalization, threshold, resolution, tool) and against external ground truth or expert judgment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a method-choice change materially alters clusters or conclusions

pros.claim: separates robust structure from method artifacts
pros.example: stability across normalizations confirms a real subfield boundary

cons.claim: full sensitivity sweeps are expensive and rarely reported
cons.example: exhaustive perturbation across all choices is combinatorial

acceptance_tests: sensitivity to key method choices reported
stability metric exceeds documented threshold or caveats stated

nodes.definition: Produce the final map narrative plus a complete reproducibility package (data query, parameters, code, versions) enabling independent regeneration.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a stakeholder needs to reproduce or audit the map

pros.claim: reproducibility makes the map auditable and trustworthy
pros.example: a logged VOSviewer config lets a reviewer regenerate the exact map

cons.claim: complete reproducibility packaging is often skipped under deadline
cons.example: GUI-only workflows leave no reproducible parameter trail

acceptance_tests: independent re-run reproduces the map within tolerance

edges.why_related: scope and unit determine which data source has adequate coverage
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scope-driven source choice avoids coverage bias
edges.example: country-level question needs Scopus affiliation coverage

edges.why_related: scope and chosen relations constrain which tool is appropriate
edges.risk_of_conflict: tool picked before scope wastes configuration
edges.example: CitNetExplorer needs a direct-citation question

edges.why_related: the chosen source export format defines the cleaning needed
edges.risk_of_conflict: cleaning before source choice is wasted
edges.example: Scopus CSV needs different reference parsing than WoS

edges.why_related: overlay maps require journal or category metadata from the source
edges.example: WoS categories feed the base map

edges.why_related: disambiguation operates on cleaned deduplicated records
edges.example: duplicate records split author identities

edges.why_related: coupling counts shared parsed references from cleaned records
edges.example: reference parse quality drives coupling strength

edges.why_related: co-citation counts co-occurring parsed cited references
edges.example: cited-reference matching depends on parsing

edges.why_related: topic models consume cleaned abstracts or text
edges.example: boilerplate removal improves LDA topics

edges.why_related: burst detection needs clean time-stamped frequency series
edges.example: misparsed years distort burst intervals

edges.why_related: co-word relies on merged keyword variants from disambiguation
edges.example: 'ml' and 'machine learning' merged before co-word

edges.why_related: co-authorship nodes are disambiguated authors or institutions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: correct identities yield correct collaboration ties
edges.risk_of_conflict: ambiguous names break the social network
edges.example: unified author ids prevent split nodes

edges.why_related: co-word counts must be normalized into similarity
edges.risk_of_conflict: raw co-word counts overweight frequent terms
edges.example: association strength normalizes the co-word matrix

edges.why_related: co-authorship ties are normalized for productivity effects
edges.example: fractional counting normalizes collaboration ties

edges.why_related: coupling strength is normalized for reference-list size
edges.risk_of_conflict: raw coupling favors long reference lists
edges.example: Salton index normalizes coupling for list length

edges.why_related: co-citation counts are normalized for citation frequency
edges.example: cosine normalizes co-citation frequencies

edges.why_related: pruning is applied to the normalized similarity network
edges.risk_of_conflict: thresholding raw counts hides weak-but-real links
edges.example: prune after association strength is computed

edges.why_related: clustering partitions the pruned network backbone
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a stable backbone gives stable clusters
edges.risk_of_conflict: clustering a noisy full graph is unstable
edges.example: a top-N backbone feeds Leiden

edges.why_related: tool defaults constrain the available clustering method and resolution
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unexamined tool default biases clusters
edges.example: VOSviewer VOS clustering and a Leiden CLI differ
edges.resolution_rule: tool clustering default must be reconciled with intended method; intended method dominates

edges.why_related: layout colors and groups nodes by cluster assignment
edges.example: VOS layout colors Leiden clusters

edges.why_related: the strategic diagram is built from cluster centrality and density
edges.risk_of_conflict: no clusters means no strategic diagram
edges.example: a Callon diagram plots each co-word cluster

edges.why_related: labels describe the produced clusters
edges.example: cluster 7 labeled after the partition

edges.why_related: temporal tracking matches per-slice cluster assignments over time
edges.risk_of_conflict: no per-slice clusters means no evolution map
edges.example: slice clusters matched across periods
edges.resolution_rule: cluster each slice before temporal tracking

edges.why_related: both are citation-based relations measuring intellectual proximity from opposite citation directions
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating the two confuses front and base
edges.example: coupling is citing-side, co-citation is cited-side
edges.resolution_rule: treat as complementary; do not merge into one matrix

edges.why_related: co-word themes and text topics both estimate conceptual structure from language
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating outputs as identical hides method bias
edges.example: BERTopic topics compared to co-word clusters
edges.resolution_rule: use as cross-validation; keep separate provenance

edges.why_related: aggressive pruning can negate normalization protection of weak-but-real links
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-pruning after normalizing discards genuine emerging links
edges.example: a high cutoff removes normalized weak ties normalization had rescued
edges.resolution_rule: normalization-protected weak links dominate: prefer lower thresholds with sensitivity testing over aggressive pruning

edges.why_related: threshold choice and clustering resolution jointly control cluster count creating tension
edges.risk_of_conflict: tuning both for a nice map risks confirmation bias
edges.example: raising threshold and lowering resolution both shrink cluster count
edges.resolution_rule: fix threshold by reproducible rule first then tune resolution; robustness test dominates aesthetic tuning

edges.why_related: full vs fractional counting in co-authorship conflicts with normalization assumptions
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing counting scheme and normalization double-corrects or undercorrects
edges.example: fractional counting plus association strength may overcorrect prolific authors
edges.resolution_rule: choose counting and normalization as a coherent pair; dominance to methodological consistency

edges.why_related: disambiguation error rate changes the stability and validity of the final map
edges.example: merge errors create unstable hubs across runs
edges.resolution_rule: improve disambiguation when robustness is low

edges.why_related: the normalization measure changes cluster sensitivity and thus robustness
edges.example: clusters identical under cosine and association strength are robust

edges.why_related: resolution and algorithm choice change partition stability feeding robustness
edges.example: Leiden seed variance quantified in robustness

edges.why_related: robustness failure triggers revisiting the normalization choice
edges.example: instability across measures sends the analyst back to normalization
edges.resolution_rule: revisit normalization until clusters stabilize or are reported as method-dependent; stop after one documented sweep

edges.why_related: robustness failure triggers re-running clustering with new resolution or seeds
edges.example: an unstable partition sends the analyst back to clustering
edges.resolution_rule: re-cluster with adjusted resolution; stop after the stability threshold is met or after 3 attempts

edges.why_related: expert label disputes can trigger re-clustering at a different resolution
edges.example: experts say a cluster mixes two themes so recluster finer
edges.resolution_rule: re-cluster only if expert disagreement is material; stop after experts accept labels or after 2 iterations

edges.why_related: bursts flag candidates whose full trajectory is then tracked temporally
edges.example: a burst term is followed across slices
edges.resolution_rule: detect bursts before deep temporal tracking

edges.why_related: overlay footprint indicators feed the final portfolio report
edges.risk_of_conflict: reporting before overlay omits the footprint
edges.example: an interdisciplinarity score is added to the report
edges.resolution_rule: compute overlay before the final report

edges.why_related: robustness validation checks whether labeled clusters survive method perturbation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: labeled clusters are the validation targets
edges.example: robustness confirms the 'gene editing' cluster persists

edges.why_related: the report must carry the robustness and sensitivity findings and caveats
edges.benefit_of_coupling: robustness results make the report honest
edges.example: sensitivity caveats included in the limitations
edges.resolution_rule: complete robustness before the final report

edges.why_related: the rendered map is the central figure of the report
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the map figure anchors the report
edges.example: the final VOSviewer figure is embedded in the report

conflict_axes.trigger: raising thresholds to make a readable map removes weak-but-real emerging links
resolution_order: set threshold by a reproducible rule
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: robustness dominates aesthetics: never drop links whose removal flips conclusions without disclosure
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no threshold yields both legibility and stable clusters
conflict_axes.example: a high min-occurrence cut hides a nascent research front

conflict_axes.trigger: different similarity measures yield different clusters from the same counts
resolution_order: justify the measure for the relation type
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: method-appropriate measure dominates: pick the measure matching the relation and disclose sensitivity
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if clusters are unstable across all reasonable measures
conflict_axes.example: cosine vs association strength shift cluster boundaries

conflict_axes.trigger: resolution parameter trades the modularity resolution limit against over-splitting
resolution_order: pick the most stable interpretable level
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: interpretability with stability dominates a single default resolution
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if experts and modularity disagree on granularity
conflict_axes.example: a default resolution merges two genuine subfields

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing one citation-based relation hides the structure the other reveals
resolution_order: match relation to the question (front vs base)
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: question-fit dominates: coupling for current fronts, co-citation for the intellectual base
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the question needs both front and base simultaneously
conflict_axes.example: coupling shows recent fronts while co-citation shows classics

conflict_axes.trigger: counting scheme and normalization can double-correct or undercorrect productivity
resolution_order: choose counting and normalization as a coherent pair
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: methodological consistency dominates: avoid mixing schemes that double-correct
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a hyperauthorship paper dominates the network
conflict_axes.example: fractional counting plus association strength overcorrects prolific authors

conflict_axes.trigger: GUI-only convenience leaves no scriptable parameter trail
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reproducibility dominates convenience: an auditable trail is mandatory
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a map cannot be regenerated from logged inputs
conflict_axes.example: VOSviewer GUI clicks leave no reproducible trail

conflict_axes.trigger: author keywords and text topic models give different thematic structures
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: data-fit dominates: use topics when keywords are sparse, cross-validate when both exist
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if co-word and topic maps contradict materially
conflict_axes.example: BERTopic finds sub-themes that index keywords miss

conflict_axes.trigger: sensitive burst parameters or end-of-window effects flag spurious emergence
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: confirmed trajectory dominates: a burst counts only if temporal tracking supports it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if many bursts cluster at the data edge
conflict_axes.example: a recent partial-year spike registers as a spurious burst

conflict_axes.trigger: naive top-term labels mislead while expert labeling is costly
resolution_order: draft labels from top terms and representatives
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: expert-validated labels dominate for decision-grade maps
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if experts reject auto labels for key clusters
conflict_axes.example: a top-term label 'cell' hides a clinical-vs-battery ambiguity

edge_cases.trigger: an edge or workflow step references a node id that was renamed or removed
edge_cases.example: an edge points to a deleted relation node
edge_cases.detection_method: resolve every edge from/to and dependency against the node id set

edge_cases.trigger: the normalization-vs-pruning tradeoff is encoded as a dependency instead of a conflict
edge_cases.failure_mode: a real tradeoff is hidden and dominance logic is lost
edge_cases.example: pruning tension modeled as a prerequisite edge
edge_cases.detection_method: check that tradeoff pairs have a conflict edge with signed_tension<0 and a resolution_rule
resolution: keep the dependency for the build-order relation

edge_cases.trigger: a feedback relation is mislabeled as a dependency creating a cycle
edge_cases.failure_mode: no valid topological order for execution
edge_cases.example: label->cluster modeled as dependency instead of feedback
edge_cases.detection_method: DFS cycle check over dependency edges plus node dependencies
resolution: convert the weaker edge to feedback

edge_cases.trigger: a metric is hand-edited without recomputing derived scores
edge_cases.failure_mode: final_importance or risk_score diverges from its formula
edge_cases.example: risk_if_wrong changed but risk_score not updated
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute all derived fields and compare within tolerance 0.02

edge_cases.trigger: a node with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 lacks acceptance tests or human review
edge_cases.failure_mode: a high-risk step is finalized without a gate
edge_cases.example: a clustering node finalized without stability tests
edge_cases.detection_method: for each high-risk node assert non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required true

edge_cases.trigger: a node with cross_topic_coupling>=0.75 lacks revisit triggers
edge_cases.failure_mode: upstream change does not propagate a revisit
edge_cases.example: scope change does not trigger downstream revisit
edge_cases.detection_method: for each high-coupling node assert non-empty revisit_triggers

edge_cases.trigger: a value is labeled observed or experimentally_validated without supplied data
edge_cases.failure_mode: unsupported empirical claim violates evidence governance
edge_cases.detection_method: scan all label fields for observed or experimentally_validated

edge_cases.trigger: a downstream artifact is hard-locked before robustness validation passes
edge_cases.example: the report locked before sensitivity testing
edge_cases.detection_method: verify no hard_lock precedes dependency, validation, and human-review gates

edge_cases.trigger: a threshold removes the emerging structure the study targets
edge_cases.failure_mode: the phenomenon of interest is pruned away
edge_cases.example: a min-occurrence cut hides the burst term
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether targeted terms survive the threshold; report removed-fraction
resolution: lower the threshold for targeted entities

edge_cases.trigger: non-deterministic clustering yields different partitions across seeds
edge_cases.failure_mode: conclusions depend on a single lucky seed
edge_cases.example: Leiden gives different clusters per seed
edge_cases.detection_method: run multiple seeds and compute partition agreement (e.g. NMI)
resolution: aggregate or fix the seed and disclose

edge_cases.trigger: a template placeholder survives into the populated KB
edge_cases.failure_mode: unresolved placeholder text breaks machine consumption
edge_cases.example: a template claim token survives unedited in a node pro field
edge_cases.detection_method: scan raw text for the placeholder token set

workflow.objective: fix scope, unit of analysis, time window, and the tool
workflow.do_first_because: scope and unit are the highest-coupling, highest-irreversibility foundations all downstream steps depend on

workflow.objective: select and justify the data source against the scope
workflow.do_first_because: source coverage caps what the map can ever show, so it must be fixed before extraction

exit_criteria: record set and entity registry frozen
workflow.do_first_because: disambiguation errors propagate into every relation, so identities must be stabilized early

workflow.objective: build the chosen co-occurrence and citation relations
entry_criteria: record set and entity registry frozen
outputs: term, collaboration, coupling, and co-citation matrices
acceptance_tests: each matrix matches its relation definition
workflow.do_first_because: relations must exist before they can be normalized; choosing the right relation prevents full rework

workflow.objective: normalize counts and prune to a backbone
workflow.do_first_because: normalization and thresholds determine cluster structure, so they are set before clustering

workflow.objective: detect clusters and lay out the map
workflow.do_first_because: clustering is the highest-risk inferential step and must be stabilized before interpretation

workflow.objective: detect emergence and track thematic evolution
workflow.do_first_because: dynamics build on stable per-slice clusters and add the time narrative
interpretation requires finished clusters and must precede validation of the labeled structure

workflow.objective: test sensitivity to method choices and validate against expert judgment
workflow.do_first_because: validation must complete before any finalization so artifacts are not locked on artifacts

workflow.objective: produce the final narrative and reproducibility package
acceptance_tests: independent re-run reproduces the map within tolerance
workflow.do_first_because: delivery is last and may hard-lock only after dependency, validation, and human-review gates pass

priority_rationale.notes: root foundation all steps depend on

dominance_rules.trigger: a method shortcut speeds delivery but risks an invalid map
dominance_rules.rule: never accept a shortcut that fails robustness validation
dominance_rules.example: skip sensitivity testing rejected because clusters were seed-dependent

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is ready before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: do not finalize a node before its dependencies are reviewed
dominance_rules.example: clustering not run before normalization despite its importance

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks eligible evidence
dominance_rules.rule: keep heuristic labels and zero observed fields when no data exists
dominance_rules.required_action: label as heuristic; set observed_impact and data_quality to 0.0
dominance_rules.example: a weight kept heuristic rather than labeled observed

dominance_rules.trigger: validation has not finished but a lock is requested
dominance_rules.rule: no hard lock before validation passes
dominance_rules.example: report kept soft until robustness completes

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible step is about to finalize
dominance_rules.rule: require human review for high-risk nodes and irreversible delivery
dominance_rules.required_action: route to human reviewer with a decision record
dominance_rules.example: clustering and report require human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: adding more objects threatens schema consistency
dominance_rules.rule: preserve schema consistency over adding objects
dominance_rules.required_action: reject objects that break the schema
dominance_rules.example: drop a near-duplicate node rather than bend the schema
trim an example string to keep valid JSON

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim exceeds what sources support
dominance_rules.rule: every claim must resolve to a source or be downgraded
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence_refs or remove the claim
dominance_rules.example: an observed-sounding claim downgraded to heuristic

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient GUI workflow is not reproducible
dominance_rules.required_action: export configuration or script the pipeline
dominance_rules.example: scripted pipeline chosen over GUI-only clicks

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient edge would create a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker edge to feedback with a stop condition
dominance_rules.example: label->cluster modeled as feedback not dependency

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve scope and unit before selecting the data source
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a source chosen for the wrong unit forces re-extraction
anti_rework_rules.example: Scopus chosen then scope shifts to a WoS-only field

anti_rework_rules.rule: lock the source before cleaning records
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: cleaning started before the source is locked
anti_rework_rules.example: WoS parser run on a Scopus export
duplicates split one author into many

anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: relation matrices built before identities frozen

anti_rework_rules.rationale: thresholding raw counts hides weak-but-real links
anti_rework_rules.example: weak normalized ties cut before normalization

anti_rework_rules.rationale: clustering a noisy full graph is unstable
anti_rework_rules.example: unstable partition from an unpruned graph

anti_rework_rules.rule: finish clustering before labeling and diagrams
anti_rework_rules.rationale: interpretation of shifting clusters is wasted
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: labels written before partition is stable

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete robustness before finalizing or locking
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking an unvalidated map forces a full redo
anti_rework_rules.example: conclusions retracted after late sensitivity analysis

anti_rework_rules.rule: populate formula inputs before computing scores
anti_rework_rules.rationale: scores computed from missing inputs are inconsistent
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: derived scores present without their inputs

iteration_protocol.trigger: the validator or a sensitivity test reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report and stability deltas to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk_score and downstream impact
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect may have wide downstream effects
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependency and feedback edges from the defect node

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
a repair changed a locked or high-coupling component
iteration_protocol.detection: rerun the validator and affected acceptance tests

iteration_protocol.trigger: new sensitivity evidence shifts a node's importance
iteration_protocol.detection: compare posterior delta to the revisit threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible decision cannot be auto-resolved
a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare counts, references, and formula consistency against the prior version
acceptance_tests: no new reference or formula failures

checks.repair_action: kept normalization<->pruning tradeoff as a separate conflict edge
scores computed by formula script within tol 0.02

change_triggers: new data source or coverage change
version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked structural change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
